programs.title: The Extraordinary States of Procopius
programs.desc: Marcin Prokop sets off on another journey around the United States.Together with cameraman Bebek, he will lie on the beaches in Miami, see historic plantations in Georgia and party in the clubs of New Orleans.

programs.title: Woman at the end of the world
programs.desc: Malta is a small but picturesque island country located in the Mediterranean Sea.Every year, makeshift boats and rafts come to its shores, bringing over three thousand refugees fleeing war, hunger and human trafficking.Only the strongest survive the journey in terrible conditions.Then they have to drift for up to forty days along the sea border because no one wants to accept them.Martyna Wojciechowska meets Hermon from war-torn Eritrea, and Agnes from Zimbabwe.The former did not intend to come to Europe, but when she became pregnant, she had no choice - it was the only way to ensure the safety of herself and her daughter.The second was a victim of human trafficking.She hasn't seen her children for five years.She works hard to become independent and create a new home for her family.

programs.title: Woman at the end of the world
programs.desc: This is the unique, 100th edition of the program whose main character is Elżbieta Dzikowska.She is a sinologist, journalist, art historian and photographer, but she is most famous as a traveler.Together with Tony Halik, she discovered the farthest, wildest corners of the Earth for Poles at a time when they practically could not cross the border of their country.It was she who made Martyna Wojciechowska, who was just a few years old, start dreaming about expeditions.Many years later, the women met and became friends, but so far they have not had the opportunity to go on a journey together.Now the situation has changed, and the destination of the escapade is Podlasie.

programs.title: Woman at the end of the world
programs.desc: This season was special in many ways.It included the 100th anniversary episode, produced for the first time in Poland.At the same time, this series was considered the most difficult, because due to the pandemic, Martyna Wojciechowska had to stay in the country for four months, and further photos might not have been taken at all.However, for both the traveler and her heroines, the impossible does not exist.In the last episode, viewers will learn about the behind-the-scenes of the program, prepared during the pandemic.Despite the border closure, the team traveled a distance equal to one length of the equator, meeting truly extraordinary women.

programs.title: Woman at the end of the world
programs.desc: The Roma live in most countries, but do not have their own country.According to estimates, there are from 8 to 15 million of them in the world, and in Romania - from about 500,000 to 2 million.Among the many Roma communities, we can mention the Gabors, who traditionally have the same surname to honor the Hungarian king from whom they received rights in the 17th century.They are referred to as aristocracy due to their light skin and financial status.They are distinguished by their attachment to tradition and the Adventist church.Men wear hats and mustaches.If they do not have the latter, it means that they have renounced their origins.Women, on the other hand, must hide their hair from marriage until death, and cannot wear makeup, lipstick or long nails.Their beauty lies in their naturalness.Although individual families traditionally pursue specific professions, they run the home.Martyna Wojciechowska, however, meets Rosalina in Transylvania, who is learning crafts in her future father-in-law's workshop.

programs.title: Taste the world with Pascal
programs.desc:
Master chef Pascal Brodnicki shows viewers how to replace traditional dishes with Asian dishes.It proves that preparing an original dinner is simple and does not have to cost much.In search of culinary inspiration, he goes to Vietnam, Laos and Thailand.He shops at local markets, prepares and sells snacks on the street, and works on a rice plantation.To prove himself, he prepares exotic dishes for his Asian hosts.He tries grilled gecko and baked ant larvae, and accepts an invitation to an unusual hunt
The next stop on Pascal Brodnicki's culinary journey is Laos, whose cuisine is famous for its unusual ingredients.Flowers, insects, frogs, tadpoles, insect cocoons, lizards, geckos and even squirrel meat are eaten here.Fried seaweed, khai pene, is the culinary trademark of Luang Prabang, a city located in the north of the country.In Laos, hundreds of families earn their living by harvesting seaweed.The traveling chef found out what their job is all about.For several hours he collected algae from the bottom of the Mekong, then cut them and rolled them into long sheets.

A traveling chef learns about the peculiarities of southern Vietnam.Hanoi is a place where different cultures meet.The restaurants serve delicacies known all over the world, such as egg omelette.Seafood is popular, including huge snails weighing several kilograms.The main export of this part of Vietnam is ngoc mam fish sauce.Pascal Brodnicki will have the opportunity to present his culinary skills in difficult conditions.At a street eatery in Saigon, he will prepare three dishes in five minutes.
